gcs_object_names.json: provenance

What it is
  Python's google-cloud-storage 3.6.0 (requests 2.32.5), for 31 object names: Blob.public_url
  (python_public_url), blob._quote of the name (python_quoted, the JSON API's path segment and
  query value), the DELETE request it prepares after requests/urllib3 normalized the URL, or
  the ValueError it raises instead (python_delete), and the JSON token naming the object in its
  multipart upload's metadata, json.dumps with ensure_ascii (python_metadata_name). Requests are
  captured by a requests adapter that answers them itself: nothing is sent.

Where it comes from
  Repository  slaudio (github.com/charliek/slaudio)
  Branch      feature/rust-h1-cleanup-scheduler at cc841b980c866c1982d366e3a326af6ba7010746
  Path        backend-rs/tests/fixtures/dispatch/gcs_object_names.json
  Added in    9fa32a5169b9836c6b1b7ff2ec89bf39379a903d ("feat(rust): dispatch pieces ...")
  Generator   backend-rs/scripts/fixtures/gen_dispatch.py, gcs_object_names() and GCS_NAMES
              (make -C backend-rs fixtures), run on slaudio's backend virtualenv (Python 3.13.15)
  sha256      5174269d386f6750651575fe3dac7c6130b15a7d841ed123bafb827224dfa6dc

  Copied byte for byte (same sha256). Before the copy, gcs_object_names() was rerun on its own
  from that generator against the same virtualenv (2026-10-20): the 31 cases and the version
  fields came out equal to this file's.

How it is used (plan 024, C4)
  crates/gcp/tests/storage.rs, the "golden names" tests:
  - ObjectNamePolicy::Strict refuses the 14 names it refused in v0.8.0, with no request and no
    token, and sends the 17 others with Python's encoding;
  - public_url_with(.., Literal) equals python_public_url for all 31;
  - under Literal, delete's path equals python_delete's (its query aside) for every case but
    "", "." and "..", which are refused; Python refuses "" too, and sends "." and ".." to
    rewritten paths ("/o/" and the bucket itself) that no client should send;
  - under Literal, both uploads send all 31 names: the media upload's name= is python_quoted, and
    the multipart metadata's name parses to the same string as python_metadata_name (serde_json
    writes non-ASCII raw where json.dumps escapes it: equal as JSON, not as bytes).

Updating it
  Regenerate in slaudio, never edit here, and copy the new file and its sha256 in together.
